title: The algorithm is only one boundary
question: What can an attacker observe or disturb without breaking the mathematical algorithm?
scenario: A hardware-backed signing service uses an approved algorithm. Remote clients see different error codes and response-duration bands for invalid requests. The service also runs on shared hardware, and technicians can reach a maintenance port. The team has no evidence yet that a secret leaked or that any attack succeeded.
focalRelation: Intended input and output cross the service interface, while timing, errors, cache effects, and power or electromagnetic effects are possible observations; an induced fault travels inward. A possible path is a review target, not proof of leakage or exploitation.

nodes.label: Remote service interface
nodes.detail: A remote requestor supplies an untrusted signing request and observes the documented response, error, and duration.

nodes.label: Signing computation
nodes.detail: Approved algorithm executes with secret-dependent state inside the conceptual implementation boundary.

nodes.label: Timing and error surface
nodes.detail: Remote observers may compare response duration bands and externally distinguishable failures.

nodes.label: Shared cache surface
nodes.detail: A co-resident workload may measure cache effects if isolation and scheduling permit observation.

nodes.label: Power and EM surface
nodes.detail: A physically capable observer may measure power or electromagnetic behavior near the device.

nodes.label: Maintenance-port disturbance
nodes.detail: A technician or other capable actor may inject a disturbance through the maintenance interface and alter computation without following the intended input path.

lanes.label: Documented interface
lanes.rule: Solid INPUT/OUTPUT paths carry intended data only.

lanes.label: Implementation boundary
lanes.rule: The boundary encloses computation and secret-dependent state; it does not claim physical isolation.

lanes.label: Possible outward observations
lanes.rule: Dashed OBSERVE paths identify measurable surfaces, not proven secret exfiltration.

lanes.label: Possible inward disturbance
lanes.rule: DISTURB enters execution and remains distinct from observation.

states.title: Start with the intended interface
states.caption: A request enters, computation runs, and a result leaves. Algorithm approval establishes no claim about observable implementation behavior.

statuses.computation: The approved algorithm is identified, but the deployed implementation has not yet been assessed against the stated attacker model.
statuses.interface: A remote requestor supplies an untrusted signing request and observes the documented response, error, and duration.

states.title: Remote observation surface
states.caption: Different external errors and duration bands are measurable. Test whether they depend on sensitive state before claiming leakage.

statuses.timing-errors: Response timing and errors are remotely observable, although the evidence does not yet establish exploitable leakage.
statuses.interface: A remote requestor supplies an untrusted signing request and observes the documented response, error, and duration.
statuses.computation: Approved algorithm executes with secret-dependent state inside the conceptual implementation boundary.

states.title: Attacker model changes the surface
states.caption: A co-resident workload can make cache behavior relevant; physical proximity can make power or EM behavior relevant. Neither follows from the remote case alone.

statuses.cache: Cache behavior requires review when an attacker can plausibly run a co-resident workload.
statuses.power-em: Power and electromagnetic leakage require review when physical measurement is credible.
statuses.computation: Approved algorithm executes with secret-dependent state inside the conceptual implementation boundary.

states.title: Fault injection points inward
states.caption: Maintenance access may allow an induced fault. Physical controls, debug-port authorization, safe error handling, and result validation protect a different path from observation.

statuses.fault: Maintenance access creates a possible disturbance path, although no successful fault has been demonstrated.
statuses.computation: Approved algorithm executes with secret-dependent state inside the conceptual implementation boundary.
statuses.interface: A remote requestor supplies an untrusted signing request and observes the documented response, error, and duration.

states.title: Controls follow the measured path
states.caption: Normalize relevant errors, evaluate constant-time techniques for the timing path, isolate shared resources, protect maintenance access, and retest the actual build under the stated attacker model.

statuses.computation: The deployed build requires assurance testing against each credible observation or disturbance path.
statuses.timing-errors: The team normalizes externally visible errors and measures timing across controlled inputs.
statuses.cache: The team isolates shared resources and tests the deployed build for cache-dependent leakage.
statuses.power-em: The team evaluates shielding, emissions, power behavior, and the physical attacker model.
statuses.fault: The team restricts maintenance access, hardens fault responses, and detects abnormal disturbances.

variants.label: Remote caller
variants.changedFact: The observer has only network access.

states.title: Remote evidence
states.caption: Measure external duration and errors under controlled inputs; cache, power, and physical fault paths are not granted by this attacker model.

statuses.timing-errors: This observation path is in scope for the stated attacker model.
statuses.cache: A network-only caller has no established co-resident cache-observation path.
statuses.power-em: A network-only caller has no established physical power or electromagnetic observation path.
statuses.fault: A network-only caller has no established physical fault-injection path.
statuses.interface: A remote requestor supplies an untrusted signing request and observes the documented response, error, and duration.
statuses.computation: Approved algorithm executes with secret-dependent state inside the conceptual implementation boundary.

variants.label: Co-resident workload
variants.changedFact: A workload controlled by the reviewer shares the host after a compiler update.

states.title: Build and observer changed
states.caption: Reassess cache behavior and isolation for the new build; normalized network errors do not settle the shared-resource surface.

statuses.cache: Shared-cache observation is in scope, but the evidence does not yet prove leakage.
statuses.timing-errors: The previous remote-timing result remains specific to that observation surface.
statuses.computation: Approved algorithm executes with secret-dependent state inside the conceptual implementation boundary.

variants.label: Physical maintenance access
variants.changedFact: A technician can reach the device and maintenance interface.

states.title: Physical assurance
states.caption: Review power/EM observation and inward fault paths, protect the debug interface, and validate behavior after disturbances.

statuses.power-em: Power and electromagnetic observation are in scope for the physical attacker model.
statuses.fault: Fault injection is in scope because the technician can reach the device and maintenance interface.
statuses.computation: Approved algorithm executes with secret-dependent state inside the conceptual implementation boundary.

prediction.prompt: The service uses a strong algorithm but exposes distinguishable errors and durations. Which assurance action comes first?

options.label: Dismiss the remote timing signal because side channels are assumed to require local probes or physical contact.
options.feedback: Remote callers may observe duration and error differences. Physical access is relevant to other surfaces, not a prerequisite for every side channel.

options.label: Replace the cryptographic algorithm immediately without measuring whether implementation behavior depends on secret state.
options.feedback: The observation is tied to implementation behavior. A new algorithm can retain the same externally distinguishable path.

options.label: Define the remote observer, measure the behavior, and test sensitive-state dependence
options.feedback: Correct. The evidence must connect an authorized observation to sensitive state before the team selects a path-specific control or claims leakage.

prediction.hint: Compare distributions under controlled inputs; one fast sample does not establish leakage.

transfer.prompt: Errors are normalized, but a compiler update changes cache behavior on a shared host where a co-resident workload is in scope. What follows?

options.label: Reassess cache behavior and isolation for the new build without presuming a leak
options.feedback: Correct. Test the relevant observation path and sensitive-state dependence; a compiler change is a trigger to assess, not proof of exploitation.

options.label: Declare the signing key compromised because cache behavior changed
options.feedback: A behavior change does not prove useful leakage, attacker capability, or key recovery. Gather build-specific evidence first.

options.label: Keep the earlier result because normalized errors close the implementation boundary
options.feedback: Error normalization addresses one surface. The build and observer changed, so the cache path needs its own assurance.

transfer.hint: Change the secret-dependent operation while holding the measurement method constant.

retry.prompt: Network and cache tests show no sensitive-state dependence, but an unattended debug port can alter clock voltage during signing. Which review is now decisive?

options.label: Reuse the negative network tests because all implementation paths share one result
options.feedback: Negative observation tests do not assess an inward disturbance through a physical maintenance interface.

options.label: Authorize a fault-injection review and harden, monitor, and validate the maintenance path
options.feedback: Correct. The changed fact introduces an inward disturbance path requiring physical, hardware, coding, and result-validation controls.

options.label: Accept the port because the approved algorithm detects every induced fault
options.feedback: Algorithm approval does not establish safe behavior under induced faults or protect an unattended debug interface.

retry.hint: Look for repeatable separation beyond noise before claiming a side channel.

takeaway: Model the observer and direction of each path. Intended I/O, outward observation, and inward disturbance require different evidence and controls; none alone proves an attack succeeded.
assumptions: The boundary is conceptual and does not assert physical isolation.
No scale, exploit probability, or attack success is represented.
Constant-time techniques address relevant timing behavior but do not eliminate every cache, power, error, or fault risk.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: Implements the accepted computation cutaway with distinct intended, observation, and disturbance grammars plus synchronized attacker-model states.
Carries the reviewed prototype’s remote, co-resident, and physical focus cases, compiler-change transfer, non-exploit caveat, and no-iframe semantic model into production data.
